cards.text: Charts: no shellcheck in the gate. Four shell scripts now carry the repo's real logic, one of them constrained to POSIX sh for the alpine/helm CI container, and nothing enforces that constraint automatically — the dash check was manual.

HelmCharts: collect_version_dependencies.py runs `helm get values` for every discovered release with no namespace-exists guard - the guard resolve_helm_args.get_helm_args:95-97 does have - so a release that never installed (the pre-image window this slice opens) aborts version-poller runs repo-wide, killing drift detection for all ~45 releases rather than skipping one. Hardening it is a HelmCharts change outside this slice.

Architecture model: the new charts/charts chart, the charts-prd namespace and the charts.home ApplicationService are absent from docs/architecture/helm-charts.yaml - architecture.yaml is deliberately not written per HelmCharts' standing instruction, so the update-architecture agent owes a run once the release is deployed.
Charts is a new repo carrying only the .kubecoder/project.yaml this slice landed: no CLAUDE.md, no spec repo, no dev-pipeline onboarding. Worth /dev:onboard before it takes slices of its own.
Charts: tests/publish.sh check 1's stale-tarball remedy only names 'bump the version in Chart.yaml' — carded only if the fix round does not reword it alongside the package-chart.sh skip.

Charts: tests/publish.sh:82's rewritten-tarball remedy names `git checkout -- dist/`, which does not clear a staged rewrite (`M `) — the same check flags it, the remedy leaves status unchanged, and the gate stays red. Minor, self-limiting; carded if not taken in passing.

HelmCharts: origin/main moved two commits past the slice base while the run was executing (e87150d, touching charts/nginx/files/snippets/proxy.conf and scripts/setup-env.sh). The P3 commit 053ddab is 'ahead 1, behind 2', so the operator's push is rejected as non-fast-forward until `git pull --rebase`. No conflict — P3 only adds new paths under charts/charts/ and configs/prd/charts/.

Charts: the recorded order 'create IaC/Charts and run it once BEFORE the test phase pushes Charts' is not executable. pvginkel/Charts exists on GitHub but is empty (git ls-remote returns zero refs), so a Pipeline-from-SCM build has no main to check out, fails before any Groovy runs, and properties() never registers githubPush(). Workable order: create the job -> test phase pushes -> operator manually runs IaC/Charts once (this is the build that produces the image V11 needs) -> pushes thereafter auto-trigger.

Charts: containerTemplates.helm (alpine/helm:3.9.1, run as a sleep-infinity sidecar) has no other user across the checked-out estate — IaC/Charts' first build is the first exercise of that container template, not just of the Helm 3-vs-4 indexing gap P2 recorded. If it misbehaves the fallback is one line: containerTemplates.modern_app_dev, which carries Helm 4.

Ansible repo: origin/main has diverged from this pod's local main (last common ancestor a8506f5) via a large amount of unrelated concurrent work (iac-agent/jenkins-agent history, latest at 9c035bd, timestamped after this slice's 7db7610). This slice's own Ansible commit ('Added new repos.', 7db7610 — just `.kubecoder/config.yaml` + workspace file, no infra content) was therefore left unpushed rather than force-rebasing a shared, actively-moving branch on my own initiative; it isn't required for any of this slice's acceptance criteria. Worth the operator's attention next time Ansible main needs reconciling.

Pre-existing, unrelated to this slice: `poetry run resolve-helm-args .` (repo-root/JSON mode) crashes with an uncaught RuntimeError instead of degrading gracefully when `helm`/cluster access fails for an unrelated release (hit this for trello-mcp-prd, version-poller-prd, webathome-org-prd, zigbee2mqtt-prd — this pod's read-only kubeconfig can't list Secrets in those namespaces). `process_release()` only catches `ImageResolutionError`, not this class of failure. Did not affect verification of the `prd/charts` release specifically (probed with the single-release invocation instead), and `resolve_helm_args.py` is untouched by this slice's diff.

HelmCharts: `resolve-helm-args prd/charts .` is no longer runnable from this pod now that charts-prd exists — the namespace-exists guard passes, `helm get values` is then denied by the read-only kubeconfig (cannot read release Secrets), and get_helm_args:107 raises an uncaught RuntimeError. Same defect as the test phase's carded pre-existing finding, but it now also hits the single-release invocation the P3 done-record names as its gate, so a later agent following that record will read a permissions crash as a broken release. Pre-image it 404'd instead; nothing in this slice's diff caused either.

Charts: the nginx:alpine base layer's stock `index.html` and `50x.html` still ship in the served docroot — both confirmed 200 on the live https://charts.home. Cosmetic only (helm fetches /index.yaml and the tarball URLs, never these), and the P2 r1 reviewer already logged it as advisory; a one-line `RUN rm` in the Dockerfile closes it whenever the repo is next touched. Note the P3 plan bullet's related prediction is falsified live: `/` returns 404, not the welcome page, because `location / { try_files $uri =404; }` bypasses the index directive.

Still open, pre-existing and unrelated to this slice's diff (resolve_helm_args.py untouched): `resolve-helm-args prd/charts .` now that charts-prd exists crashes with an uncaught RuntimeError from this pod's read-only kubeconfig being unable to read release Secrets via `helm get values` (process_release() only catches ImageResolutionError, not this class). Hits the exact single-release invocation P3's done-record names as its gate — a later agent following that record would read a permissions failure as a broken release.

Cosmetic, still live: the base nginx image's stock `/index.html` and `/50x.html` remain in `charts-home`'s served docroot (both 200) because `COPY dist/ /usr/share/nginx/html/` merges into rather than replaces the base layer's docroot. Helm only ever fetches `/index.yaml` and the absolute tarball URLs, so this has no functional effect; `/` itself answers 404 (try_files bypasses the index directive), which falsifies the P3 plan's own prediction that `/` would show the welcome page but is otherwise inert. A one-line `RUN rm` in the Dockerfile closes both, whenever that file is next legitimately touched — not eligible for this round's mechanical-residue exception since it is a behaviour change, not formatting.

history.summary: Charts gains charts/homelab-shared (library, 0.1.0): the eight HelmCharts helpers copied under the homelab-shared.* prefix, and the Terraform PreSync hook Job as homelab-shared.tf-presync-hook with the estate pin hook.imageTag: "1" in the library's values. The repo also earns its gate: .kubecoder/project.yaml (root component, jenkins: IaC/Charts) lints the library and runs tests/render-consumer.sh, which renders tests/consumer — a fixture taking the library as its one dependencies: entry — and asserts all nine surfaces plus the prefix's negative case. kc project lint and kc project test are green; HelmCharts is untouched.

The library chart lands its outcome: eight helpers copied verbatim under the homelab-shared.* prefix (diffed against the HelmCharts source), the PreSync hook Job matching design.md:331-357 field for field, the quoted R5 pin reaching a consumer through the coalesced values key, and HelmCharts untouched. No gate was recorded, so I ran it — lint and test green from the repo root — and probed it rather than trusting it: the pin assertion and the prefix negative test both bite under mutation, and the one unguarded value (the image tag) fails loudly rather than silently when coalescing is broken. Two Minor advisory findings only: unignored helm-dependency artifacts under tests/consumer/, and ceph PVC coverage limited to the legacy inline-PV branch.

Charts now publishes: dist/ is the committed store (homelab-shared-0.1.0.tgz), tools/build-index.sh regenerates the Helm index over it with absolute https://charts.home URLs, and the Dockerfile bakes tarballs plus index into nginx:alpine; the Jenkinsfile indexes in containerTemplates.helm, pushes registry:5000/charts-home under :<build> and :latest, and calls cicd.helmDeploy(). tests/publish.sh gates that dist/ is the sources packaged and that re-indexing is additive (V07, proven by execution) — all its checks and both Dockerfile guards confirmed to bite by mutation; kc project lint/test/build all green.
root: cexec iac tests/publish.sh    [  OK  ]

P2 delivers its outcome: a committed dist/ store, a full-directory helm repo index with absolute https://charts.home URLs, an nginx:alpine image baking both, and a Jenkinsfile pushing :<build>+:latest through helmCharts.kaniko2 then triggering IaC/HelmCharts. Verified beyond the gate by running the uncovered `kc project build` (green) and by two mutation probes. Three Minor advisory findings, none blocking: the base image's stock index.html/50x.html survive into the served root (so `/` is not the 404 P3's plan text assumed — plan.md corrected), the gate lets an already-published tarball be silently rewritten, and tools/package-chart.sh is never executed by anything.

charts.home lands as an ordinary HelmCharts release on phase/006-P3: chart charts/charts/ (static nginx on registry:5000/charts-home, port 80, helpers symlink, no homelab-shared dependency) plus configs/prd/charts/{_shared/infrastructure.tf,prd/values.yaml}, modelled on tfmirror. Proven through the repo's own deploy CLI — deploy config derives release/namespace charts-prd with phases.infra true, deploy template renders the Service and Deployment, resolve-helm-args builds registry:5000/charts-home:latest (404 until the operator's IaC/Charts build publishes it, which is V11's expected pre-image state), terraform fmt -check clean. Commit is local: pushing HelmCharts deploys straight to prd and is the operator's keystroke.

The diff transposes the tfmirror model onto the ruled names correctly, and I reproduced every property the phase rests on by execution: deploy config gives charts-prd with phases.infra true, deploy template renders exactly the Service and Deployment against registry:5000/charts-home, terraform fmt is clean, and resolve-helm-args builds the reference and 404s as the expected pre-image state. R4 holds (no dependencies: at all), V19 holds (real mode-120000 symlink), V04 holds trivially (nothing existing is touched), and the consumed interface matches what P2 actually publishes. No Blockers or Majors; two advisory Minors recorded, neither changing the diff.

R1-R5 are all delivered and every acceptance criterion has implementing work I can point at, except the live-endpoint ones (V06, V11-V14, V18) which are the test phase's and the operator's by design, not owed by a phase. No done-record admits a leftover and no phase depends on something nothing produced. What is outstanding is four gaps the merged work exposed inside the two gate scripts this slice wrote, each named by a phase review as an advisory Minor and each a few lines: tests/publish.sh claims 'a published version is immutable' in its own header but passes an already-published tarball that has been silently rewritten (demonstrated by the P2 reviewer) - which is exactly the property D17's dependencies: pins and a consumer's Chart.lock rest on, and the reason this slice exists; tools/package-chart.sh is the one new executable nothing runs, with publish.sh re-implementing it instead; the ceph PVC helpers are rendered only on their legacy inline-PV branch, never the TF-owned one the B.1 migrations will use; and a hand-run `helm dependency update tests/consumer` writes two unignored files. Appended as P4 (Target ../Charts). Everything else advisory or out of scope is carded; no mechanical residue to fix (the diff is whitespace-clean, all four scripts parse, build-index.sh is dash-clean).

Closed all four gate gaps on phase/006-P4: published-version immutability is now enforced against git in both halves (working tree and history), tests/publish.sh repacks through tools/package-chart.sh (which gained an optional destination argument), the consumer fixture renders the ceph helpers' TF-owned-PV branch and the claimName override, and .gitignore covers what a hand-run `helm dependency update tests/consumer` writes. kc project lint, test and build are green from the repo root, and every new assertion was confirmed to bite by mutating the thing it defends — including the P2 reviewer's exact previously-green rewrite sequence. Nothing the repo publishes changed: dist/, Dockerfile, Jenkinsfile, the manifest and HelmCharts are untouched.
root: cexec iac tests/publish.sh    [  OK  ]

All four named gaps are genuinely closed and I re-derived the executor's mutation claims independently; nothing the repo publishes moved. Two Majors, both advisory: tools/package-chart.sh repacks every chart, so the new immutability check condemns the repo's own publish command (demonstrated red on a no-op repack with misleading remediation text, and permanently red in history once a second chart is published), and both immutability checks silently vacate when git exits non-zero while the gate still prints its success line (demonstrated: the P2 reviewer's exact tamper sequence passes green with no .git). One Minor: one refute assertion cannot be tripped by a mutation of the branch it guards, so the done-record's blanket bite claim overstates.

All three findings resolved on phase/006-P4 (6fbfbbe). tools/package-chart.sh now skips a version the destination store already holds, so the repo's own publish command no longer rewrites published tarballs and no longer condemns itself through the new immutability check — verified across a bare run, a second-chart publish (green through commit) and a legitimate version bump. tests/publish.sh runs each git command outside the `|| true` that absorbs grep's no-match, so a git that cannot answer aborts the gate under set -e instead of printing the success line (verified: .git removed → exit 128, no success line), and the rewritten-tarball remedy now names restoring rather than a spurious bump. Finding 3 was prose: the done-record's blanket "every new assertion confirmed to bite" is narrowed to record that the TF-owned rbd refute cannot be tripped by its branch mutation (helm errors first) — confirmed by execution. lint, test and build green from the repo root.
root: cexec iac tests/publish.sh    [  OK  ]

Both round-1 Majors are genuinely closed — verified by re-running the demonstrations: the gate now exits 128 on a git that cannot answer (both git calls, not just the first), and a bare or multi-chart `tools/package-chart.sh` no longer rewrites an already-published tarball. The fix to package-chart.sh introduces the mirror problem: its skip is unconditional on git-tracked-ness, so an uncommitted tarball is never refreshed either, and check 1's stale remedy then walks a developer into permanently publishing a version whose bytes match no committed source state. That skip also has no coverage at all — deleting it leaves the whole gate green.

Finding 1 is blocking on the review's own evidence and I re-derived its premise from the code: tools/package-chart.sh:32-36 skips on mere existence ([ -e ]), while tests/publish.sh:80 deliberately exempts '??' and 'A[ M]' because a tarball git does not yet carry has never been served and is free to change. The skip is broader than the property it defends, it is new in 6fbfbbe (git diff a2e4304..6fbfbbe confirms the block did not exist before), and check 1's remedy text then names the one action that cannot work — walking a developer into committing a permanently-published, immutable-by-the-new-check chart version whose bytes match no committed source state. That is a wire-contract artifact a consumer pins against via index.yaml and Chart.lock, which is squarely the round-2 bar. Finding 2's missing coverage rides along as part of landing the fix — the phase set its own mutation bar at plan.md:399-400 and the new conditional is exactly the assertion-free behaviour change that bar exists to catch; Finding 3 is one string in a file the executor is already editing, so take it if trivial, otherwise it cards.

All three r2 findings resolved on phase/006-P4 (012a266). tools/package-chart.sh now skips only a version HEAD carries at the destination's own path (git -C "$DEST" ls-tree), so an untracked tarball repacks — the reviewer's package-then-edit sequence is green at every step and the committed 0.1.0 tarball stays byte-identical — while a git that cannot answer aborts the run instead of rewriting served bytes. tests/publish.sh gates both halves of that skip (bare run against the real dist/, restored byte for byte either way; truncated scratch store that must refill), each confirmed to bite: deleting the skip reddens the first, reverting it to [ -e ] reddens the second. Check 1's stale remedy and the rewritten-tarball remedy (git checkout HEAD -- dist/, verified to clear a staged M ) both name a fix that works. kc project lint, test and build green from /work/Charts; done-record updated.
root: cexec iac tests/publish.sh    [  OK  ]

All three round-2 findings re-derived as closed on a clone of 012a266: the skip is git-scoped and the package-edit-repack loop is open again, both halves of it now bite under mutation (deleting the skip and reverting it to [ -e ] each redden the gate), and 'git checkout HEAD -- dist/' verifiably clears a staged rewrite. The fix commit introduces no blocking problem; two advisory Minors — a done-record bullet whose causal claim the fix falsified, and the gate's deliberate mutate-and-restore of the real dist/ whose backup the EXIT trap owns.

No done-record admits an unaddressed leftover: P4's one recorded exception (the TF-owned rbd refute cannot be forced to bite, because the mutation errors the render first) is explained and the regression is still caught as a red render. Nothing depends on something no phase produced, and there is no mechanical residue — git diff --check is clean in both repos, all four scripts pass bash -n and build-index.sh passes dash -n — so I made no edits and nothing needed committing. Two operator-sequencing findings from this pass are carded rather than appended: they need no code, but the second one changes the order of the keystrokes P2's done-record records.

Executed docs/slice-testing-strategy.md for slice 006. All 19 verification.json criteria checked with a verdict + evidence each: 16 verified — largely by re-running the Charts repo's own gates myself (tests/render-consumer.sh, tests/publish.sh, helm lint, plus a re-read of the already-green kaniko `--no-push` build log) rather than trusting the established GREEN sweep alone, and by read-only live probes (`resolve-helm-args`, `deploy config`/`deploy template` against HelmCharts, DNS lookup, registry:5000 tag probe). No idempotence/check-mode/blast-radius/cluster-serial concerns apply — the slice's only Ansible-repo change is `.kubecoder/config.yaml` + workspace file registering new repos, no ansible/terraform content touched. No product defect found; nothing clears the generation bar. Pushed `Charts` to origin/main (new branch — pre-authorized, dev-tier, non-prod). Per the plan's explicit ruling, HelmCharts (053ddab, 'P3: charts.home as an ordinary HelmCharts release') was deliberately NOT pushed — that is the operator's keystroke. V12/V13/V14 (live DNS+TLS, end-to-end Helm-client resolution against charts.home) are correctly OWED, not verified: the `IaC/Charts` Jenkins job does not exist yet (confirmed via the Jenkins API — no job at that path), so even though Charts is now on origin, nothing has built or published `registry:5000/charts-home` yet (confirmed 404 on both the registry and `resolve-helm-args`), and `charts.home` does not resolve (NXDOMAIN). This is the expected pre-deploy state the plan itself anticipated, not a slice defect.

Operator steps owed, in order (the ordering matters — image before deploy):
1. Create the Jenkins job `IaC/Charts`: Pipeline script from SCM, repo `https://github.com/pvginkel/Charts.git`, branch `*/main`, credentials `5f6fbd66-b41c-405f-b107-85ba6fd97f10`, script path `Jenkinsfile`. Then run it once by hand (Build Now) — `Charts` is already on origin/main, so this build packages+indexes dist/, pushes `registry:5000/charts-home:1` and `:latest`, and (via `cicd.helmDeploy()`) triggers a HelmCharts deploy — harmless at this point since HelmCharts main does not yet carry the `charts` release.
2. Once that build is green and the image exists: `cd /work/HelmCharts && git push origin main` — deploys commit 053ddab, which creates namespace `charts-prd` (TF infra apply), installs the `charts` release (image now resolves), and applies TF config. This is the prd-mutating step and stays operator-gated regardless of the devlock, per the plan's explicit ruling ('the test phase pushes Charts but MUST NOT push HelmCharts').

After both land, V12/V13/V14 can be settled by: `curl -sk https://charts.home/index.yaml` (or `helm repo add homelab https://charts.home && helm repo update && helm search repo homelab/homelab-shared`) and a DNS lookup for both `charts.home` and `charts`.
